title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Comprehensive Reference
author: Ava Patel
content:
Overview

This document is a consolidated reference for private deployments of Redwood Inference (VPC-hosted and on-prem). It covers reference architectures, packaging options, pre-deployment customer requirements, day-2 operational procedures, and upgrade/rollback playbooks. Intended audience: solutions engineers, infra engineers, SREs, and customer platform teams.

Table of contents
1) Scope and Intent
2) Ownership and SLAs
3) Supported Deployment Modes
4) Customer Requirements (quick reference table)
5) Reference Architectures
6) On-Prem Packaging and Air-Gap Options
7) VPC Deployment Guide (step-by-step)
8) Day-2 Operations and Monitoring
9) Upgrade & Rollback Procedures (playbook)
10) Troubleshooting Matrix and Runbook Links
11) Appendices (samples: Terraform, K8s, checks)

1) Scope and Intent
- Consolidate operational guidance for VPC and on-prem private deployments offered to enterprise customers.
- Provide a single source of truth: networking, security, packaging, installation, day-2 ops, and upgrade/rollback.
- Not a vendor-specific hardware procurement guide; refer to customer-specific reference architecture pages for exact SKU lists.

2) Ownership and SLAs
- Product owner: Priya Singh (Product) — primary contact for feature and packaging changes.
- Engineering owner: Infrastructure / Private Deployments team (team: eng-private-deployments).
- SRE oncall: private-deployments-sre rotation.
- Typical SLA targets (for Dedicated/Private customers):
  - Uptime SLO: 99.9% per month (customer-specific in contract)
  - 95th percentile inference latency target: per-catalog model profile (see model-catalog).
  - Change windows: standard business hours unless otherwise contracted.

3) Supported Deployment Modes
- VPC-managed control plane with customer VPC data plane (recommended for most enterprise customers).
- Private managed (Redwood runs control plane in customer VPC).
- Fully on-prem (air-gapped) packaged bundle — customer runs both control plane and data plane in their datacenter/Kubernetes cluster.

4) Customer Requirements (quick reference table)
- The following table maps minimum requirements we use when qualifying a private deployment opportunity. Use the customer requirements library to generate a tailored checklist.

ASCIITable: Minimum Requirements by Tier
| Requirement                     | Minimum (Dev)      | Recommended (Prod)        | Notes/Checks                   |
|---------------------------------|--------------------|---------------------------|--------------------------------|
| Kubernetes version              | 1.22               | 1.24+                     | control-plane and node versions|
| Nodes (GPU)                     | 1 x A10-equivalent  | 4 x A100/8 x A10           | model-dependent; see sizing table|
| CPU-only nodes                  | 2 x 8vCPU          | 4 x 16vCPU                | for control-plane services     |
| Disk (per node)                 | 500GB SSD          | 1TB NVMe                  | model and caching dependent     |
| Network (throughput)            | 1 Gbps             | 10 Gbps                   | low-latency RDMA for high throughput|
| Storage for model artifacts     | 500GB              | 5TB                       | S3-compatible object store recommended|
| KMS/HSM                        | optional            | required (enterprise)      | KMS integration for customer keys|
| Outbound connectivity (control) | required            | required                  | for control-plane telemetry and license checks|

5) Reference Architectures
- Lightweight VPC reference (small teams): 3 subnets (control, compute, management), NAT + egress rules, internal ALB for routing, private registry in management subnet.
- Production VPC reference: Multi-AZ, private control-plane with high availability, autoscaling compute pools for inference, dedicated KV cache layer, optional GPU burst pool in a separate AZ.

Architecture diagram (textual):
- Management VPC: Bastion / Ops jump, private registry, metrics ingest (Prometheus remote write to customer TSDB optional).
- Control Plane (private): API gateway (internal), orchestration services (k8s control-plane / operators), RBAC backed by customer IdP (OIDC/SAML), KMS integration.
- Compute Plane: GPU node pools, autoscaler, persistent cache (redis/managed) in same AZ for latency.
- Networking: ENIs per node for bandwidth isolation, ingress restricted to control-plane subnets, egress via NAT Gateway with customer egress IPs.

6) On-Prem Packaging and Air-Gap Options
- Packaging formats provided:
  - OCI images (preferred) hosted in customer registry.
  - Tarball artifact (air-gap) with checksum + signature.
  - Helm chart + CRDs or Operator bundle for Kubernetes installs.
- Air-gap install flow (high level):
  1. Customer provides offline registry or local container registry VM.
  2. Redwood provides signed tarball containing images, charts, manifests, licensing blobs, and an installation script.
  3. Customer loads images into registry: `ctr images import images.tar` or `docker load -i images.tar`.
  4. Run `./redwood-install.sh --airgap --namespace redwood` from bastion.
- Packaging checklist:
  - All images signed (cosign) and checksums included.
  - Offline operator manifests for CRDs and ValidatingWebhookConfiguration with proper CA certs.
  - Migration tooling for existing data volumes.

7) VPC Deployment Guide (step-by-step)
Pre-deployment checklist:
- Confirm customer CIDR ranges and colliding IPs.
- Verify required IAM roles and service principals exist.
- Ensure customer KMS details and certificate signing options are provided.
- Confirm outbound egress policy allows control-plane telemetry endpoints.

High-level steps:
1) Network & IAM provision (Terraform snippet shown in Appendix).
2) Customer provisions EKS/GKE/AKS cluster or provides access to existing k8s cluster.
3) Deploy Redwood control-plane chart into management namespace with values.yaml customized to customer network and registry.
4) Configure model storage (S3-compatible or NFS) and point control-plane.
5) Install compute pools: create GPU node pools using customer preferred instance types and node labels.
6) Run validation suite (see Appendices) and baseline performance benchmark.

Example: minimal Helm install command
`helm repo add redwood https://packages.redwood-inference.internal/charts`
`helm upgrade --install redwood-control-plane redwood/control-plane \\`
`  --namespace redwood-system \\`
`  -f values.customer.yaml \\`
`  --wait --timeout 15m`

8) Day-2 Operations and Monitoring
- Monitoring stack recommendation: Prometheus + Grafana (local) with remote write to customer TSDB for long term retention.
- Essential dashboards: nodes (GPU/CPU utilization), model inference latency (p50/p95/p99), queue lengths, KV cache hit rate, request error rate, per-model cost breakdown.
- Backups and restores:
  - Control-plane etcd snapshots (if running k8s control plane on customer infra) — daily snapshot policy.
  - Model artifacts stored in object storage with lifecycle policies.
- Scaling and capacity planning:
  - Autoscaling policies: per-model target utilization (default 70% GPU utilization).
  - Burst pools: create a separate GPU pool labeled `burst=true` with pre-warmed instances.
- Maintenance windows and patching:
  - Regular kernel/security patch schedule: quarterly by default, monthly for high-security customers.
  - Node draining playbook: annotate nodes, cordon, drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`, replace, and requeue.

9) Upgrade & Rollback Procedures (playbook)
Principles:
- All upgrades should be performed via Helm/Operator releases and follow canary first, then staged rollout.
- Keep a reproducible snapshot of pre-upgrade state (manifests, configmaps, CRs, PVCs).

Pre-upgrade checklist:
1) Confirm backup snapshot exists (etcd, model storage manifest).
2) Ensure no active model uploads or large imports running.
3) Validate available capacity for canary nodes.
4) Run health check script and record outputs.

Canary upgrade steps (recommended):
1) Label a small subset of control-plane pods/nodes with `upgrade=canary`.
2) Apply new helm chart to canary namespace/instances: `helm upgrade --install redwood-control-plane ... --set canary.enabled=true`.
3) Run smoke tests (see Appendix B) including: API health endpoint, sample generation against pinned model, KV cache warmup, and latency regression tests.
4) Observe metrics for 30-60 minutes; if errors or regressions > threshold (error rate > 1% or p95 latency regression > 20%), abort and rollback.

Full rollout steps:
1) If canary passes, incrementally roll out to 25%, then 50%, then 100% by changing node pool labels or by updating the helm release with batch sizes.
2) Monitor; pause between batches for at least one observation window (30-60 minutes).

Rollback procedure (fast path):
1) If significant regressions are detected, perform immediate rollback: `helm rollback redwood-control-plane <previous_revision>`.
2) If traffic routing requires reversion, switch traffic back to previous model variants via the routing policy API.
3) Recreate pre-upgrade snapshot if it was removed.
4) Post-mortem: open a change incident and tag with `upgrade-failure`.

Notes on database/schema migrations:
- All DB migrations are performed under a feature flag and must be reversible. Migration playbooks live in `confluence/eng-private-deployments/migrations`.

10) Troubleshooting Matrix and Runbook Links
- Common symptom: Node-level OOM on GPU pods
  - Probable causes: model cache growth, incorrect resource limits, or memory leak in runtime.
  - First steps: check pod events, `kubectl top pod`, inspect logs at /var/log/redwood/runtime.log.
- Common symptom: High p95 latency
  - Probable causes: saturated network, cold KV cache misses, insufficient batching.
  - First steps: check KV cache hit rate dashboard, inspect network metrics, increase batching window for low-QPS models.

Runbook links:
- Private deployments runbook: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-runbook-2026-03-10
- Upgrade & rollback playbook (detailed): /confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-vpc-onprem-upgrade-rollback-playbook-2026-06-01

11) Appendices
Appendix A — Sample Terraform (network) snippet
`resource "aws_vpc" "redwood" {\n  cidr_block = var.vpc_cidr\n  tags = { Name = "redwood-vpc" }\n}\n# Example: create private subnets per AZ, NAT gateway, route tables...`

Appendix B — Validation and Smoke Tests (automated)
- `scripts/validate-cluster.sh` will perform:
  1) API health endpoint check: `curl -sS https://redwood-control-plane.internal/health`
  2) Generate test inference with a tiny model and assert response schema and latency < 500ms for dev sizing.
  3) KV cache warmup check: request same prompt 3x and confirm hit rate > 50% on second/third call.
